outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Attention Bottleneck in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the Transformer architecture and the computational challenges associated with the attention mechanism, setting the stage for the need for hardware-aware optimizations.
subtopics: The Transformer Architecture and the Multi-Head Attention (MHA) Mechanism
Complexity Analysis: The Quadratic Scaling Problem with Sequence Length
Applications of Long-Context Modeling (Codebases, High-Resolution Images, Video)
Evolution of Attention Optimization: From Approximation to Software Optimization
Introduction to FlashAttention: The Core Philosophy of Memory-Efficient Tiling

outline.chapter_title: Foundations: GPU Hardware and Execution Models
outline.description: To understand FlashAttention-3, students must first understand the underlying hardware. This chapter covers the NVIDIA Hopper architecture and the principles of high-throughput computing.
subtopics: GPU Memory Hierarchy: Global Memory (HBM), L2 Cache, Shared Memory (SMEM), and Registers
Thread Hierarchy: Threads, Warps, Threadblocks, and Clusters
Hardware Acceleration Units: Tensor Cores and the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA)
The Concept of Asynchrony: Overlapping Data Movement and Computation
Low-Precision Arithmetic: The Shift from FP16 to FP8 and its Hardware Implications

outline.chapter_title: The Evolution of FlashAttention: From Version 1 to 2
outline.description: This chapter traces the lineage of FlashAttention, explaining how previous iterations solved memory bottlenecks and where they hit a performance ceiling on modern hardware.
subtopics: FlashAttention-1: Tiling and Fusing to Minimize Memory Reads/Writes
FlashAttention-2: Parallelizing over Sequence Length and Block-wise Matrix Multiplication
The Utilization Gap: Why FlashAttention-2 Underperforms on Hopper H100 GPUs
Synchronous vs. Asynchronous Execution Models in Kernel Design

outline.description: This chapter dives into the first major technical contribution of FlashAttention-3: using producer-consumer models to hide latencies.
subtopics: Warp-Specialization: Dividing Warps into Producers (Data Movement) and Consumers (Computation)
The Producer-Consumer Pipeline with Circular Shared Memory Buffers
Asynchronous Data Movement with TMA and WGMMA Instructions
Pingpong Scheduling: Overlapping Softmax Computation with Matrix Multiplication
Register Management: Using 'setmaxnreg' for Dynamic Allocation

outline.chapter_title: Advanced Pipelining: Overlapping GEMMs and Softmax
outline.description: This chapter explains the intra-warpgroup optimizations that break sequential dependencies between attention operations.
subtopics: Identifying Sequential Dependencies in the Attention Inner Loop
The Two-Stage Pipelining Algorithm: Hiding Softmax under Asynchronous WGMMA
Register Pressure Trade-offs: Balancing Pipeline Depth and Tile Size
Theoretical vs. Practical Performance: Compiler Reordering and SASS Analysis
Introduction to 3-Stage Pipelining for Higher Tensor Core Utilization

outline.description: This chapter covers the third pillar of FlashAttention-3: achieving massive throughput using FP8 while maintaining numerical integrity.
subtopics: FP8 Hardware Constraints: Layout Conformance and k-major Requirements
In-Kernel Transpositions using LDSM and STSM Instructions
Register Permutation: Bridging Accumulator and Operand Layouts
The Challenge of Outliers in Large Language Models
Accuracy Preservation Techniques: Block Quantization and Incoherent Processing
Orthogonal Matrix Multiplication: Spreading Outliers without Changing Output

outline.description: The final chapter summarizes the results, comparing FlashAttention-3 against state-of-the-art baselines and analyzing the accuracy of the low-precision methods.
subtopics: Benchmarking FlashAttention-3 vs. FlashAttention-2 and cuDNN
TFLOPs/s Analysis: Reaching 75% Utilization on H100 GPUs
Ablation Studies: Quantifying the Gains from Asynchrony and Pipelining
Numerical Error Analysis: Comparing RMSE across FP16 and FP8
Conclusion: The Future of Efficient Long-Context Attention
